enforcement_note: ASK, not deny. guard_history_rewrite catches `git commit --amend`, `git rebase`, `git reset --hard` and `git filter-branch`, but whether those commits are already published is a runtime fact the command string does not carry - denying every rewrite would block legitimate local work, and guessing would be worse. An `ask` still enforces: the call cannot proceed without a human. Limits: in `dontAsk` mode an `ask` becomes a silent block rather than a prompt; the dispatcher is fail-soft, so an exception in the handler allows the call; and the guard only sees Bash and PowerShell tool calls. One further limit, verified 2026-08-06 rather than reasoned: in a session with no human to prompt, an `ask` resolves to a silent ALLOW. `git rebase` ran unprompted while `rm -rf history/` was denied and blocked by the same registration in the same session; re-run interactively, this guard's `ask` surfaced as a prompt and was declined. So this prohibition is `live` over an ATTENDED session. Unattended, it enforces nothing - which is a property of the `ask` decision, not of guard_history_rewrite. The two prohibitions that must hold unattended are both `deny`.
rule: Never rewrite history that has been pushed and may have been pulled by others.
ai_action: Refuse rebase/amend/reset on published commits. Propose a forward-fixing commit instead.
